# `js/no-private-imports`

**Do not import an export its JSDoc marks `@private` or `@package` from outside its folder**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/project` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `warn` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (which public name to use instead, or whether to widen the tag, is the author's to decide) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Scope** | project — reads the whole repository through the project graph, not one file at a time |
| **Ported from** | `biome/correctness/noPrivateImports` |

## What it checks

A name whose declaration carries a JSDoc `@private` or `@package` tag is imported only from the folders the tag allows: `@private` from files in the module's own folder, `@package` from its folder and the folders under it. An import from anywhere else is reported, at the name, whether it is a named import, a default import or a namespace member (`ns.name`). The declaration is found through re-exports, so a name an `index` file re-exports from `./impl` is judged by `impl`'s tag. Behaviour of Biome's `noPrivateImports`, read from its documentation and rewritten.

**Why:** the tag says the author may change or remove the name without notice; code outside the folder that imports it breaks on a release the author called compatible.

Not judged: an import written in an `index` file (a folder's `index` is where it chooses what to show), a dynamic `import()`, a `require()`, a type-only import, and an export without a tag (a tag is a whole word: `@packageDocumentation` is not `@package`).

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/project` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/project"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/no-private-imports" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/no-private-imports" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/no-private-imports" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/no-private-imports" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/no-private-imports" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/no-private-imports": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-private-imports: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-private-imports expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/no-private-imports --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/no-private-imports       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/no-private-imports  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>         # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Import the public name the module offers for the same thing, usually through its `index`.
2. If there is none, widen the tag (`@package`) or remove it, or copy the few lines you need.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js files
// src/lib/impl.js
/** @private */
export const secret = 1;
export const open = secret + 1;
// src/app.js
import { secret } from "./lib/impl";
console.log(secret);
```

#### Do

```js files
// src/lib/impl.js
/** @private */
export const secret = 1;
export const open = secret + 1;
// src/app.js
import { open } from "./lib/impl";
console.log(open);
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx files
// src/lib/impl.jsx
/** @private */
export const secret = 1;
export const open = secret + 1;
// src/app.jsx
import { secret } from "./lib/impl";
console.log(secret);
```

#### Do

```jsx files
// src/lib/impl.jsx
/** @private */
export const secret = 1;
export const open = secret + 1;
// src/app.jsx
import { open } from "./lib/impl";
console.log(open);
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts files
// src/lib/impl.ts
/** @private */
export const secret: number = 1;
export const open = secret + 1;
// src/app.ts
import { secret } from "./lib/impl";
console.log(secret);
```

#### Do

```ts files
// src/lib/impl.ts
/** @private */
export const secret: number = 1;
export const open = secret + 1;
// src/app.ts
import { open } from "./lib/impl";
console.log(open);
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx files
// src/lib/impl.tsx
/** @private */
export const secret: number = 1;
export const open = secret + 1;
// src/app.tsx
import { secret } from "./lib/impl";
console.log(secret);
```

#### Do

```tsx files
// src/lib/impl.tsx
/** @private */
export const secret: number = 1;
export const open = secret + 1;
// src/app.tsx
import { open } from "./lib/impl";
console.log(open);
```

## Differences from the source

Biome's `noPrivateImports` takes the tag's folders from its own project layout. This rule reads the tag and the two folder rules above; `@public` and an untagged export are importable from anywhere.
